Hi Alex,

Thanks for the intro call today — really helpful to understand Redwood's hosting options. Procurement asked me to pull together a short mutual action plan (MAP) so we can get alignment on milestones and the procurement path (we'd prefer private-offer via marketplace where possible). High-level asks from our side:

- Confirmation on which private-offer lanes you support (AWS, GCP, Azure) and any key differences in billing flow.
- An estimated acceptance timeline for a standard MAP (evaluation -> security review -> PO -> invoicing).
- Any items Redwood needs from AurumTech to unblock SOC/document review.

Can you send a one-page MAP template or a short timeline so we can review with our procurement and cloud teams? We have a target go-live window of mid-Jan 2027.

Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP + marketplace private offer options

Hi Sana — great to meet earlier. Attaching a concise MAP draft and a private-offer comparison that maps the typical billing paths for AWS vs GCP. Quick answers up front:

- Redwood supports AWS and GCP private-offers today; Azure private-offer is possible but requires a slightly different procurement flow (we can scope if you want Azure).
- Billing path differences: AWS private-offer can be routed through your AWS invoice (private offer acceptance -> Redwood invoice via AWS) which is fastest for teams that already use consolidated billing. GCP private-offer requires a partner billing flow (commit + invoice) — slightly longer acceptance time in our experience.
- For SOC / security review we typically need an NDA (if not in place), a short questionnaire (we can pre-fill the high-level answers), and an account owner confirmation for contract signature.

I put a proposed MAP timeline in the attached PDF that aims for a Dec -> Jan cadence to hit your mid-Jan go-live. Core milestones: 1) Eval kickoff and test plan (2 weeks), 2) Security review & PO draft (2–3 weeks), 3) Marketplace/private-offer acceptance + invoice route (1–2 weeks), 4) Onboarding + smoke tests (1 week).

Next steps: can Kimberly coordinate the billing details with your procurement team? Kimberly — can you confirm whether the AWS private-offer would be the shortest billing path for this account and call out any constraints we should flag?

Thanks — I attached: redwood-accelerated-mpa-draft.pdf, marketplace-private-offer-comparison.xlsx, redwood-sow-v1.docx

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-accelerated-mpa-draft.pdf (3 pages), marketplace-private-offer-comparison.xlsx (tabbed), redwood-sow-v1.docx

Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP + marketplace private offer options

Hi Sana / procurement team — looping in the billing details. Short version: if AurumTech has a preferred cloud vendor we can prioritize that private-offer lane. A few notes that affect timeline and invoicing:

- AWS Private Offer: fastest to get onto your consolidated invoice. We provide the private-offer acceptance instructions and Redwood will create/update the offer; you accept in the AWS marketplace and AWS handles the charge routing. Estimated acceptance window once legal signs: 3–7 business days.
- GCP Private Offer / Commit: works, but often requires a partner billing setup and acceptance on the partner side — this typically adds 7–14 business days.
- Azure: not recommended if you need a 2–3 week close; Azure private-offer requires a marketplace publisher flow and sometimes a reseller step.

Billing caveats: for the AWS path we can issue invoices that align to your AWS billing cycle (invoice metadata and PO references included). For GCP we often route via partner settlement which can produce a slightly delayed invoice date.

I attached a short spreadsheet that maps the acceptance window, documents required, and the typical internal owners you should loop in (cloud admin, procurement, legal).

Action items for AurumTech to accelerate:
- Confirm preferred cloud (AWS vs GCP) by EOD Friday so Redwood can generate the private-offer draft.
- Share your procurement contact + billing account ID for the chosen cloud.
- If security needs the SOC2 report, confirm the secure upload destination and we will send COC and the report.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk through the private-offer acceptance steps if that helps.

-Kimberly
Principal Product Manager, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: marketplace-private-offer-comparison.xlsx
From: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@aurumtech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sana Rao <sana@aurumtech.com>, AurumTech Procurement <procurement@aurumtech.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP + marketplace private offer options

Thanks Kimberly / Alex — quick clarifying questions from procurement: 

1) If we pick AWS private-offer, what does the PO lifecycle look like on our end? Do we sign a Redwood SOW and then accept the private-offer in AWS, or is signature handled in marketplace acceptance? We need the exact steps to map to our internal approval flow.

2) Is there any reason we should choose the partner-billing/GCP path for cost or feature reasons? Our engineering lead prefers GCP but procurement favors AWS for centralized billing.

3) Can you confirm the invoicing cadence (monthly in arrears vs monthly advance vs net-30 on invoice)? We have standard net-30 terms but can accommodate special arrangements if pre-billing through marketplace is required.

If you can respond with a short checklist for the AWS private-offer path (what we sign, where we click, who signs) that will let procurement slot this into our approval queue.

-Ravi
Procurement Manager
AurumTech
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@aurumtech.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sana Rao <sana@aurumtech.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP + marketplace private offer options

Ravi — thanks, and good questions. AWS private-offer checklist (short):

1) Redwood sends a SOW + customer-facing acceptance instructions (attached SOW v1). The SOW includes the product SKU and PO reference fields.
2) AurumTech legal / procurement reviews and countersigns the SOW (if required). If your org prefers marketplace acceptance in lieu of countersignature we accept that too — we can make the SOW reference the private-offer ID.
3) Redwood publishes a private-offer in AWS Marketplace and shares the offer ID.
4) AurumTech accepts the private-offer from the AWS account (Marketplace console) under the specified billing account ID. Acceptance routes charges to your consolidated invoice.
5) Once accepted, AWS notifies Redwood; Redwood finalizes provisioning and issues a Redwood invoice with your PO reference and agreed payment terms.

Notes on terms: our standard for marketplace private-offers is monthly billing in arrears, Net 30 (we can do Net 45 on an enterprise contract request). If you need advance billing we can discuss but that typically requires a separate contracting step.

Why pick AWS vs GCP: if procurement needs consolidated billing and fastest close, AWS private-offer is typically the shortest path. If engineering's preference for GCP is critical, we can still do GCP but expect the accept time to be longer due to partner settling (Kimberly's spreadsheet called out ~7–14 business days).

Proposed next steps (to keep to your mid-Jan go-live):
- Today: AurumTech confirms preferred cloud and provides billing account ID (Ravi).
- Mon Dec 6: Redwood sends private-offer draft & SOW reference.
- Week of Dec 6–13: Legal / procurement review.
- Week of Dec 13: Offer acceptance in Marketplace and provisioning.
- Jan 3–10: Onboarding + smoke tests.

If that timeline works, we'll prepare a DocuSign-ready SOW and the private-offer draft. I can be on the procurement call if helpful.

Thanks — Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
